metadata.title: The Supply Edge: Where a Vacuum-Tied MOND Law Must Stop for Structure Growth and Galaxy Lensing to Agree (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-07). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. Confirming simulations are running; results will be added in a new version.

We work with the law a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), kappa = 1/2 fitted, the exponential kernel nu(y) = 1/(1 - exp(-sqrt y)), and a conserved cold fluid whose amount (Omega_c/Omega_b = 5.364) is an input. In particle-mesh simulations the law's phantom over-builds small-scale structure: with a corrected pressure-filtered baryon source and a mass-conserving reservoir rule the excess at k <= 1 h/Mpc is +15.3% / +19.3% (two footings) at 256^3 and +17.4% at 512^3; about 81% of the switch-ON mass behind it lies inside host turnaround spheres. Re-fitting KiDS-1000 isolated-lens lensing with a free two-halo amplitude shows the law need only extend to x ~ 0.3-0.5 of the turnaround radius (best 0.48 / 0.53). We note that this is where a host's real cold supply runs out: the phantom mass M_ph(

Every number is checked against committed outputs by PAPER45_audit.py (11/11). kappa = 1/2 remains fitted; the cold fluid's amount and rho_Lambda are not derived; no dark-matter particle is added. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude and DeepSeek.
